sets.topic: A: 語学講座の受講形式／B: 通学時の自転車ヘルメット

partA.situation: Owen と Nadia が，スペイン語の講座をどの形式で受けるかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Owen
speakers.role: exchange student who has already chosen his format
speakers.tone: relaxed and informative, explaining the options as if reading from the course page

speakers.name: Nadia
speakers.role: student deciding which format to register for
speakers.tone: thoughtful, weighing the options aloud, warmer at the end

conversation.text: Owen, registration closes tonight and I still can't decide on the Spanish course. There are four formats, aren't there?

Four. The evening class meets on campus twice a week. The recorded course gives you video lessons you watch whenever you like. The streamed course meets online at a fixed hour. And the mixed course puts you in the classroom every other week and online the rest of the time.
I was leaning towards the evening class. I want to speak out loud, and honestly I want to meet people. Sitting alone with a laptop for a whole term sounds miserable.

I understand that, but look at what the recorded course adds. Every unit comes with a speaking bot you can argue with as long as you want, and it never gets tired of you. I found it genuinely amusing, and my accent improved more in a month than it did all last year.
A bot that doesn't sigh at my grammar. That is tempting.
And the written feedback comes back the same evening instead of the following week.
Right, I don't want to give up those extras. I'll sign up for something that includes them.
So you're joining me in the recorded course after all?
No, I still want to walk into a real classroom sometimes and hear other students trying.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Owen express about the Spanish course?
choices: Classmates are the fastest way to improve an accent.
Fixed online lessons suit busy students best.
Talking with a machine can be entertaining practice.
Written feedback matters less than speaking aloud.
q34.heard: you can argue with as long as you want
q34.explain: Owen が推しているのは recorded course の「speaking bot」です。決定打は「a speaking bot you can argue with as long as you want, and it never gets tired of you. I found it genuinely amusing」。amusing（面白い）＝ entertaining、argue with a bot ＝ talking with a machine への言い換えで③になります。本番と同じく、③の英文がそのまま読まれることはありません。
keyPhrases: a speaking bot you can argue with as long as you want
I found it genuinely amusing

distractors.why: 「人に会いたい・他の学生の声を聞きたい」は Nadia の関心です。話者の入れ替え。
fixed hour は streamed course の説明であって、Owen が勧めた形式ではありません。形式のすり替え。
Owen は written feedback の速さも利点として挙げています。「重要でない」とは言っていません。

q35.prompt: Which course did Nadia decide to take at the end of the conversation?
choices: The evening class
The mixed course
The recorded course
The streamed course

requires.cond: recorded course の追加特典（speaking bot・当日返却の添削）も手に入れたい
requires.line: I don't want to give up those extras. I'll sign up for something that includes them.

requires.cond: それでも実際の教室にも行きたい
requires.line: No, I still want to walk into a real classroom sometimes and hear other students trying.

q35.explain: Nadia は「extras も欲しい」と言った直後、Owen の「recorded course に来るの?」に No と答え、「教室にも行きたい」と言います。オンラインの特典と教室通学の両方を満たすのは、隔週で教室に出る mixed course だけです。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: 序盤の「I was leaning towards the evening class」は最後に覆されます。
Owen の「joining me in the recorded course?」に No と答えているので除外。ここで Yes と聞き違えると③になります。
streamed course は形式の説明で出ただけで、Nadia は一度も希望していません。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Colin, Riko, Bianca)が，自転車通学のヘルメットについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Colin
speakers.role: student who has never worn a helmet
speakers.tone: casual and a little defensive at first, then quieter and persuaded

speakers.name: Riko
speakers.role: student who dislikes helmets and does not change her mind
speakers.tone: light and stubborn, joking about her hair

speakers.name: Bianca
speakers.role: student who already wears a helmet every day and knows the local figures
speakers.tone: calm and factual, quoting numbers without lecturing

conversation.text: The school sent another notice about helmets today. Third one this term. I've cycled here for three years without one and nothing has ever happened, so I don't really see the point of all this paperwork.
Same here. And they flatten my hair for the entire morning, no matter what I do to it beforehand. I'm not walking into class looking like that.
I put mine on every single day, so the notice wasn't really aimed at me.
Wait, seriously? You've never once ridden without it, not even down to the shops?
Not since I started. It seems like a small thing until you look at what happens here. Last year in this city, forty-two students were taken to hospital with head injuries after bicycle crashes.
Forty-two out of how many people, though? That could be a tiny share of everyone who rides.
I looked it up because I wanted the same answer. Of every student the hospital treated after a crash, head injuries were the largest group of all. Broken arms came second, at about twenty-five.
Head injuries beating everything else, including arms and legs. That's actually the part that gets me.
It gets me too, but I still think the road near school is slow enough. If I had to wear that thing every morning, I'd rather just walk.
I think I'll start keeping one on the bike from tomorrow rather than argue with the school about it.
You'll forget it once, feel the wind on your head, and then never forget it again.
Fine, but don't expect me in one.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりもヘルメットをかぶるようにしようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前よりヘルメットをかぶるようにする

stances.evidence: I think I'll start keeping one on the bike from tomorrow rather than argue with the school about it.
stances.why: 3年間かぶっていなかったが、頭部のけがが最多という数字を聞いて「明日から持っておく」と方針が動いた。数える。

stances.evidence: Fine, but don't expect me in one.
stances.why: 数字には反応するが最後まで拒否している。「I'd rather just walk」も同方向。数えない。

stances.evidence: I put mine on every single day, so the notice wasn't really aimed at me.
stances.why: ★もともと毎日かぶっている。「以前よりも」かぶるようになる人ではない。ここを数えると②になる引っかけ。

q36.explain: 動いたのは Colin だけで1人＝①。Bianca は「every single day」もともとかぶっているので「以前よりも」には当たりません（本番2026の Vicky と同じ型）。Riko は最後まで拒否。Bianca を数えて②にするのが最大の失点パターンです。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Bianca の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.utterance: forty-two students were taken to hospital with head injuries after bicycle crashes

graphs.title: Student Bicycle Crashes by Month
graphs.measures: 月ごとの自転車事故の件数
graphs.whyWrong: 42 という数字も学生の事故も出てきますが、数えているのは「月ごとの事故件数」で、けがの種類ではありません。Bianca は頭部のけがの人数を言っています。

graphs.title: How Students Travel to School
graphs.measures: 通学手段の割合
graphs.whyWrong: 42 は「自転車通学の割合（％）」で、けがをした人数ではありません。単位が人数ではなく割合である点でも外れます。

graphs.title: Student Bicycle Crash Injuries by Body Part

axis.y: Number of students taken to hospital

graphs.measures: 自転車事故で搬送された学生のけがの部位別人数

graphs.title: Helmet Use Among Students
graphs.measures: ヘルメット着用率の推移
graphs.whyWrong: 着用率の推移で、けがの人数ではありません。42 は最終年の着用率（％）です。

q37.explain: 3点で絞ります。数字＝42／対象＝自転車事故でけがをした学生／出来事＝頭部のけがで搬送。③だけが「けがの部位別の搬送人数」を数えており、Head が 42 で最多、Arms が約25（Bianca の「Broken arms came second, at about twenty-five」）とも一致します。①②④はどれも 42 という数字は出ますが、数えているものが事故件数・通学手段の割合・着用率で別物です。

sets.topic: A: 学生寮の食事プラン／B: 教室の空調温度

partA.situation: Priya と Marco が，来学期の食事プランをどれにするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Priya
speakers.role: student who has already picked her plan and explains all four
speakers.tone: brisk and practical, like someone who has read the whole handbook

speakers.name: Marco
speakers.role: student who cannot decide and changes direction at the end
speakers.tone: hesitant, thinking out loud, decisive only in the last line

conversation.text: Priya, the meal plan form is due Friday and I've read it four times without understanding it. What are the actual choices?

Four of them. The full plan gives you three meals a day in the dining hall. The dinner plan is just the evening meal there. The credit plan loads money onto your card and you spend it anywhere on campus. And the weekday plan feeds you Monday to Friday, with weekends left to you.
The full plan sounds safest. I'd never have to think about food again, and I'd see people at every meal instead of eating alone in my room.

It's safe, but think about what the credit plan lets you do. Whatever money you don't spend rolls over to the next term instead of vanishing, and I saved enough last year to cover a whole week in Lisbon.
Money that doesn't disappear at the end of term. That is worth something.
And you can use it at the late-night cafe, which the dining hall plans don't cover at all.
Okay, I don't want to lose that rollover. I'll choose a plan that keeps it.
So you'll be on the credit plan with me?
No, I still want someone to hand me a hot dinner at the end of a long day.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Priya express about the meal plans?
choices: The dining hall serves better food than the cafe.
Eating with other students is the main benefit.
Unused funds being carried forward is an advantage.
Weekend meals are rarely worth paying for.
q34.heard: rolls over to the next term instead of vanishing
q34.explain: Priya が推すのは credit plan で、その利点として最初に挙げるのが「Whatever money you don't spend rolls over to the next term instead of vanishing」。rolls over ＝ carried forward、money you don't spend ＝ unused funds の言い換えで③です。③の英文はそのまま読まれません。
keyPhrases: rolls over to the next term instead of vanishing
you can use it at the late-night cafe

distractors.why: Priya は cafe が「dining hall plans では使えない」と言っただけで、味の比較はしていません。
「毎食people に会える」は Marco が full plan の理由として言ったことです。話者の入れ替え。
weekday plan は形式の説明で触れただけで、Priya は週末の食事について評価していません。

q35.prompt: Which plan did Marco decide to choose at the end of the conversation?
choices: The credit plan
The dinner plan
The full plan
The weekday plan

requires.cond: 使い残しが繰り越される仕組み（credit plan の要素）は手放したくない
requires.line: I don't want to lose that rollover. I'll choose a plan that keeps it.

requires.cond: それでも夕食は出してもらいたい
requires.line: No, I still want someone to hand me a hot dinner at the end of a long day.

q35.explain: Marco は「rollover は手放したくない」と言った直後、「credit plan に来るの?」に No と答え、「温かい夕食は出してほしい」と言います。夕食だけ食堂で出る dinner plan なら、残りの食費は自由に使えて繰り越しの発想も生きます。full plan（三食すべて）では繰り越す余地がありません。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: 「credit plan with me?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると①になります。
序盤の「The full plan sounds safest」は最後に覆されます。
weekday plan は Marco が一度も希望しておらず、夕食を出してほしいという条件にも直接答えません。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Devon, Hana, Tobias)が，教室の空調の温度設定について話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Devon
speakers.role: student who complains about the cold and is persuaded
speakers.tone: grumbling at first, then practical

speakers.name: Hana
speakers.role: student who decides to bring a jacket after hearing the numbers
speakers.tone: curious, asks the sharp questions

speakers.name: Tobias
speakers.role: student who already carries a jacket every day
speakers.tone: amused, quietly factual, quotes the survey

conversation.text: I could not feel my fingers in the science room this morning. Somebody upstairs has decided that eighteen degrees is a perfectly normal temperature for a classroom in the middle of June.
It's the same in the library, and in the crowded corridors it's somehow even worse. I've started writing with my sleeves pulled over my hands, which does nothing at all for my handwriting.
I keep a jacket in my bag every day of the year, so honestly I stopped noticing.
Every day? Even in the middle of summer when it's thirty degrees outside?

Especially then, because that's when they run the cooling hardest. The student council actually surveyed us about this last month, and the answers were clear. Two hundred and ten students said the rooms were too cold, which was more than any other complaint.
More than the noise complaints? People never stop talking about the noise.
Noise came second, at about a hundred and forty. Cold beat it comfortably, and everything else, the corridors and the broken lockers and the rest of it, came nowhere near.
So it isn't just me being dramatic. Two hundred and ten people are sitting there freezing.
That settles it. I'm going to keep a jumper in my locker from Monday instead of complaining about it every day.
I'll do the same. Arguing with the building manager clearly isn't working.
Welcome to the jacket club. It only took you both a year.
Don't be smug about it. You could have told the two of us all of this back in September and saved us an entire winter of misery.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも上着を持ってくるようにしようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より上着を持ってくるようにする

stances.evidence: I'll do the same. Arguing with the building manager clearly isn't working.
stances.why: 苦情を言うだけだったが、調査結果を聞いて Hana と同じく上着を用意する方向に動いた。数える。

stances.evidence: I'm going to keep a jumper in my locker from Monday instead of complaining about it every day.
stances.why: 袖を引っぱっていただけだったが、月曜から上着を置くと明言した。数える。

stances.evidence: I keep a jacket in my bag every day of the year, so honestly I stopped noticing.
stances.why: ★もともと毎日持っている。「以前よりも」持ってくるようになる人ではない。ここを数えると③になる引っかけ。

q36.explain: 動いたのは Devon と Hana の2人＝②。Tobias は「every day of the year」もともと持っているので「以前よりも」には当たりません。3人全員が最後は上着に前向きなので③に見えますが、Tobias を数えると誤りです。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Tobias の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.utterance: Two hundred and ten students said the rooms were too cold, which was more than any other complaint

graphs.title: Classroom Temperature Through the Day
graphs.measures: 時刻ごとの教室の温度
graphs.whyWrong: 測っているのは温度そのもので、人数ではありません。210 という値もどこにも出ません。

graphs.title: Students Reporting Cold Rooms by Month
graphs.measures: 月ごとに「寒い」と答えた学生の人数
graphs.whyWrong: 210 も学生の人数も合いますが、月ごとの推移であって「他の苦情との比較」ではありません。Tobias は「どの苦情より多かった」と言っています。

graphs.title: Share of Students Who Own a Jacket
graphs.measures: 上着を持ってくる頻度の割合
graphs.whyWrong: 上着を持つ頻度の割合で、苦情の集計ではありません。単位も人数ではなく％です。

graphs.title: Student Council Survey: Complaints About School Facilities
graphs.measures: 苦情の種類ごとの学生の人数

q37.explain: 数字＝210／対象＝調査に答えた学生／出来事＝施設への苦情。④だけが「苦情の種類別の人数」を数え、Cold が 210 で最多、Noise が 140（Tobias の「Noise came second, at about a hundred and forty」）とも一致します。②は210も学生も合いますが月別推移で、他の苦情と比べていません。

sets.topic: A: 卒業研究の発表形式／B: 部活の朝練の開始時刻

partA.situation: Ethan と Suki が，卒業研究をどの形式で発表するかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Ethan
speakers.role: student who has already chosen the poster format
speakers.tone: enthusiastic, speaks quickly when describing what he likes

speakers.name: Suki
speakers.role: student weighing all four formats before the deadline
speakers.tone: careful, asks short clarifying questions, firm at the very end

conversation.text: Ethan, we have to submit our presentation format by Thursday and I keep changing my mind. Remind me what the four are.

The lecture format is twenty minutes on stage in the big hall. The poster format puts you beside a printed board while people walk up and ask things. The filmed format means you record everything in advance and the panel watches it later. And the seminar format is a small room, ten people, and a discussion afterwards.
I assumed I'd take the lecture format. My whole year will be in that hall, and I want them to actually hear what I found.

That's fair, but the poster format has something the stage can't give you. Strangers come up and ask the question you never thought of, and you have to answer it right there. I left mine last year with three ideas I'd never have had alone.
Questions I haven't prepared for. That's exactly what I'm most afraid of and probably what I need.
And nobody is watching a clock, so a good conversation can run for half an hour.
All right, I'm not giving up that back-and-forth. I'll pick a format that has it.
So you'll be standing next to a poster with me on Friday?
No, I still want a proper audience sitting down and listening to the whole argument from start to finish.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Ethan express about the presentation formats?
choices: A large audience makes research feel worthwhile.
Recording in advance removes unnecessary pressure.
Short time limits force presenters to be clear.
Unexpected questions can produce useful new ideas.
q34.heard: ask the question you never thought of
q34.explain: Ethan が poster format の利点として挙げるのは「Strangers come up and ask the question you never thought of」→「I left mine last year with three ideas I'd never have had alone」。予期しない質問が新しい着想を生む、で④です。④の英文はそのまま読まれません。
keyPhrases: ask the question you never thought of
three ideas I'd never have had alone

distractors.why: 「学年全員に聞いてほしい」は Suki が lecture format を選ぼうとした理由です。話者の入れ替え。
filmed format は形式の説明で触れただけで、Ethan は録画の心理的な利点を語っていません。
Ethan は逆に「nobody is watching a clock」＝時間制限がないことを利点として挙げています。

q35.prompt: Which format did Suki decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The filmed format
The lecture format
The poster format
The seminar format

requires.cond: 予期しない質問との応答（poster format の要素）は手放したくない
requires.line: I'm not giving up that back-and-forth. I'll pick a format that has it.

requires.cond: それでも座って通しで聞いてくれる聴衆が欲しい
requires.line: No, I still want a proper audience sitting down and listening to the whole argument from start to finish.

q35.explain: Suki は「back-and-forth は手放さない」と言った直後、「poster の隣に立つの?」に No と答え、「座って通しで聞く聴衆が欲しい」と言います。10人の小部屋で発表し、そのあと討論する seminar format だけが両方を満たします。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: filmed format は録画で、質疑も生の聴衆もありません。Suki は一度も希望していません。
序盤の「I assumed I'd take the lecture format」は最後に覆されます。lecture には討論がありません。
「standing next to a poster with me?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると③になります。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Jonah, Meera, Silas)が，部活の朝練の開始時刻について話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Jonah
speakers.role: student who is always late and decides to change
speakers.tone: sheepish, then determined

speakers.name: Meera
speakers.role: student who is persuaded by the figures
speakers.tone: sharp, asks for the numbers behind the claim

speakers.name: Silas
speakers.role: student who already leaves early every day and refuses to change
speakers.tone: dry and unbothered, quotes the club record book

conversation.text: Coach moved morning practice to seven again. I only just make the old time, and that was with running the last two blocks.
I catch the seven-ten bus, so seven o'clock practice is mathematically impossible for me. Something has to change.
I leave home at six twenty every morning anyway, so the new time makes no difference to me at all.
Six twenty? Even on the mornings when there's no practice at all?

Every morning, all year. And it's worth it, because I checked the club book last week. Of everyone who missed the qualifying round over the last three years, eighty-one people missed it because of late arrival at practice, which was more than any other reason.
Eighty-one? More than injuries? I assumed injuries would be top by a long way.
Injuries came second, at about fifty-four. Late arrival was well clear of it, and illness was lower still.
So the thing most likely to keep me out of the qualifier is my own alarm clock. That is a genuinely depressing sentence.
It changes things for me too. I'll take the six forty bus from tomorrow instead of arguing about the schedule.
Then I'm setting my alarm twenty minutes earlier, starting tonight. I'd rather lose the sleep than the round.
You'll both hate me for two weeks and then stop noticing it.
We already hate you. Nobody should be that awake before seven in the morning.

q36.action: 以前より早く家を出る

stances.evidence: Then I'm setting my alarm twenty minutes earlier, starting tonight.
stances.why: ぎりぎりだったが、遅刻が予選欠場の最大要因という数字を聞いて20分早めると明言。数える。

sets.topic: A: 留学中の住まい／B: 図書館の閉館時刻の延長

partA.situation: Rosalind と Kwame が，留学中の住まいをどこにするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Rosalind
speakers.role: returning student who lived in a shared flat
speakers.tone: warm but blunt, mentions costs without softening them

speakers.name: Kwame
speakers.role: student choosing housing for next year
speakers.tone: cautious, repeats what he hears to check it, resolves late

conversation.text: Rosalind, housing applications open Monday and I have four boxes to choose between. What did they actually mean by all of them?

The hall gives you a single room on campus with a canteen downstairs. The homestay puts you with a local family and they cook for you. The shared flat is four students, one kitchen, and rent split four ways. And the studio is your own tiny place off campus with nobody else in it.
I had the studio circled. I write at strange hours and I hate explaining myself to anyone about it.

I understand, but the shared flat gave me something a studio never could. Rent split four ways came to less than half what the studio costs, and I ate properly because somebody was always cooking something.
Less than half. That's a whole extra term of savings, put like that.
And when I got ill in February, three people noticed within a day.
Right, I don't want to lose that cheaper rent. I'll apply for something that keeps it.
So you're taking a room in a shared flat like I did?
No, I still want someone older around who notices when I've stopped eating properly.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Rosalind express about the housing options?
choices: Campus canteens save more time than cooking does.
Living alone helps students concentrate on writing.
Local families teach the language faster than students do.
Sharing a kitchen can be cheaper and healthier.
q34.heard: Rent split four ways came to less than half
q34.explain: Rosalind が shared flat の利点として挙げるのは「Rent split four ways came to less than half what the studio costs」（安い）と「I ate properly because somebody was always cooking」（食生活が良くなった）。この2点をまとめた④が正解です。④の英文はそのまま読まれません。
keyPhrases: Rent split four ways came to less than half
I ate properly because somebody was always cooking something

distractors.why: canteen は hall の説明で触れただけで、Rosalind は時間の節約について評価していません。
「変な時間に書く／干渉されたくない」は Kwame が studio を選ぼうとした理由です。話者の入れ替え。
homestay の語学面の利点は、この対話では誰も述べていません。

q35.prompt: Which type of housing did Kwame decide to apply for at the end of the conversation?
choices: The hall
The homestay
The shared flat
The studio

requires.cond: 安い家賃（shared flat の要素）は手放したくない
requires.line: I don't want to lose that cheaper rent. I'll apply for something that keeps it.

requires.cond: それでも年上の誰かが体調に気づいてくれる環境がほしい
requires.line: No, I still want someone older around who notices when I've stopped eating properly.

q35.explain: Kwame は「安い家賃は手放さない」と言った直後、「shared flat を取るの?」に No と答え、「年上の誰かに気づいてほしい」と言います。学生同士の shared flat では「年上」になりません。食事が出て年上の家族がいる homestay だけが両方を満たします。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: hall は一人部屋で、年上の誰かが常にいる環境ではありません。Kwame は一度も希望していません。
「taking a room in a shared flat like I did?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると③になります。
序盤の「I had the studio circled」は最後に覆されます。studio は最も高く、誰も気づいてくれません。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Naoki, Freya, Otto)が，図書館の閉館時刻について話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Naoki
speakers.role: student who studies at a cafe and grumbles before agreeing
speakers.tone: sceptical, complains about the library, then quietly gives in

speakers.name: Freya
speakers.role: student who agrees with everything but does not change her own habit
speakers.tone: friendly, agreeable, vague about herself

speakers.name: Otto
speakers.role: student who found the survey figures
speakers.tone: matter-of-fact, slightly amused by the others

conversation.text: They're extending the library to eleven at night from next month. I thought the two of you would be pleased about that.
Not especially. I've been working in the cafe on the corner all year because the library closed before I even got started.
The cafe is nice, though. Nobody glares at you for opening a packet of crisps in there.

Fair, but the university asked people why they stopped using the library, and the answer wasn't crisps. Of everyone who said they'd given up on it, a hundred and sixty people named the closing time, which was ahead of every other reason.
A hundred and sixty for the closing time? I would have guessed noise, honestly.
Noise came second, at about ninety. Closing time was well clear of it, and lack of desks was lower again.
That's a strong argument, actually. If the hours were the real problem, then fixing the hours fixes most of it.
I suppose I can't complain about the closing time and then ignore it when they change it.
That does sound like the trap you've walked into, yes.
Fine. I'll move back in there from next month rather than pay four pounds a night for a coffee I don't drink.
Good for you. I'll keep cheering from the cafe, obviously. My table by the window has my name on it now.
So you agree with all of it and change nothing. That's very consistent of you.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも図書館で勉強しようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より図書館で勉強する

stances.evidence: I'll keep cheering from the cafe, obviously.
stances.why: ★「強い議論だ」と同意しているので数えたくなるが、自分はカフェのまま。同意は行動ではない。数えない。

stances.evidence: I thought the two of you would be pleased about that.
stances.why: ★延長を知らせる側で、もともと図書館の利用者。「以前よりも」使うようになる人ではない。数えない。

q36.explain: 動いたのは Naoki だけで1人＝①。引っかけが3人ぶん仕込まれています。Naoki は不満げな口ぶりですが結局戻る（数える）、Freya は同意するだけで動かない（数えない）、Otto はもともと利用者（数えない）。「賛成した人数」を数えると②や③になります。

sets.topic: A: 部活の練習試合の会場／B: 学食のトレー返却

partA.situation: Tariq と Elodie が，部活の練習試合をどの会場で行うかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Tariq
speakers.role: team captain who has compared all four venues
speakers.tone: organised, slightly impatient, gives figures without being asked

speakers.name: Elodie
speakers.role: vice-captain who must book the venue today
speakers.tone: practical, thinks about the players rather than the budget, decides last

conversation.text: Tariq, I have to book the venue for the practice match today. Talk me through the four again, slowly.

The school gym is free but the ceiling is low. The city arena is proper height and has seating, but it costs eighty pounds an hour. The park courts are outdoors and free, and completely at the mercy of the weather. And the community centre is indoors, half the arena price, with a small balcony for spectators.
I'd assumed the school gym. It's free, it's five minutes from the classrooms, and nobody has to travel anywhere.

Except the ceiling. Every high serve we practise in there dies against the roof, so we arrive at real matches having never played a proper lift. The arena fixed that for us in one afternoon last year.
So the gym is quietly teaching us the wrong game. I hadn't thought about it like that.
And a real ceiling means the visiting team takes us seriously from the first point.
Fine, I won't book anywhere with a low roof. It has to be full height.
So I can tell the arena we're coming on Saturday?
No, we still cannot spend eighty pounds an hour out of a budget that has forty left in it.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Tariq express about the venues?
choices: A low ceiling damages the way the team practises.
Playing outdoors builds stronger concentration.
Spectator seating raises the level of play.
Travel time matters more than facilities do.
q34.heard: Every high serve we practise in there dies against the roof
q34.explain: Tariq が school gym を否定する根拠は「Every high serve we practise in there dies against the roof, so we arrive at real matches having never played a proper lift」。低い天井が練習の質を損なう、で①です。①の英文はそのまま読まれません。
keyPhrases: Every high serve we practise in there dies against the roof
having never played a proper lift

distractors.why: park courts は「天候に左右される」と説明しただけで、屋外の利点は誰も述べていません。
Tariq は「相手校が真剣に見る」と言いましたが、その根拠は ceiling で、seating の効果ではありません。
「教室から5分・誰も移動しなくていい」は Elodie が school gym を推した理由です。話者の入れ替え。

q35.prompt: Which venue did Elodie decide to book at the end of the conversation?
choices: The city arena
The community centre
The park courts
The school gym

requires.cond: 天井が低い会場は避ける（＝屋内で十分な高さがある）
requires.line: I won't book anywhere with a low roof. It has to be full height.

requires.cond: それでも1時間80ポンドは出せない
requires.line: No, we still cannot spend eighty pounds an hour out of a budget that has forty left in it.

q35.explain: Elodie は「低い天井は避ける」と言った直後、「arena を予約していい?」に No と答え、80ポンドは無理だと言います。屋内で十分な高さがあり、arena の半額の community centre だけが両方を満たします。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: 「tell the arena we're coming?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると①になります。
park courts は屋外で、そもそも「天井の高さ」という条件の外にあります。Elodie は希望していません。
序盤の「I'd assumed the school gym」は、天井の話で自ら覆します。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Callum, Yuna, Piers)が，学食のトレーの返却について話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Callum
speakers.role: student who leaves trays on the table and is persuaded
speakers.tone: casual, defensive at first, then honest about it

speakers.name: Yuna
speakers.role: student who sets a condition that is never met
speakers.tone: reasonable-sounding, always finds one more objection

speakers.name: Piers
speakers.role: student who found the canteen's own count
speakers.tone: calm, reads the numbers off his phone

conversation.text: The canteen has put up another sign about returning trays. That's the third one this term, which rather suggests the first two didn't work.
I leave mine, I'll admit it freely. There's always someone clearing tables anyway, so it never really felt like it mattered much.
I'd return mine happily if the racks weren't right beside the entrance. Walking back against everyone coming in is genuinely unpleasant at half past twelve.

They counted it properly this month, though, and the numbers are worse than I expected. Of all the trays left behind in one week, four hundred and thirty were abandoned during the lunch hour, which was more than any other time of day.
Four hundred and thirty in a single week? At lunchtime alone?
Breakfast came second, at about a hundred and ninety. Lunch was well ahead of it, and the evening was lower still.
That is a lot of trays. Fine, I'll do it the day they move the racks to the far wall.
They said last year that they have no plans to move them at all. The plumbing runs behind that wall.
Then my offer stands exactly as it is.
I can't defend mine any more, honestly. I'll carry my own tray over from tomorrow instead of waiting for someone else to do it.
I've taken mine back since first year, so I'll just keep quietly doing that.
You've been unbearably right for this entire conversation, you know.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも自分でトレーを返そうと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より自分でトレーを返す

stances.evidence: I'll carry my own tray over from tomorrow instead of waiting for someone else to do it.
stances.why: 放置派だったが、昼の430枚という数字を聞いて明日から自分で返すと明言。数える。

stances.why: ★1年次からもともと返している。「以前よりも」返すようになる人ではない。数えない。

q36.explain: 動いたのは Callum だけで1人＝①。Yuna は「やる」と言いますが条件（ラックの移動）が満たされないので数えません。Piers はもともと返しているので「以前よりも」に当たりません。Yuna の一言だけ拾うと②、3人とも前向きに聞こえるので③に見えるのが罠です。

basis.event: trays abandoned by time of day

sets.topic: A: 文化祭の出し物／B: 職員室前の廊下の走り

partA.situation: Imogen と Hugo が，文化祭でクラスの出し物を何にするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Imogen
speakers.role: festival committee member who knows all four options
speakers.tone: cheerful and quick, sells her favourite option hard

speakers.name: Hugo
speakers.role: class representative who has to report the decision tonight
speakers.tone: worried about the quiet classmates, firm in the final line

conversation.text: Imogen, I have to report our class decision tonight. What are the four things we're allowed to do?

The food stall sells something simple all day. The stage play is twenty minutes in the hall with a proper audience. The exhibition fills our classroom with things people walk around and look at. And the escape room turns the classroom into a puzzle that visitors book a slot for.
I was going to say the food stall. It's easy, everyone can help, and nobody has to stand up in front of strangers.

It's easy, but look at what the escape room does for us. Every single person gets a job, and the shy ones end up writing puzzles instead of performing. Last year's team said the quiet members did the best work of anyone.
So the people I'm worried about would actually have the most to do. That flips my whole assumption.
And because visitors book slots, we know exactly how many people are coming and when.
All right, I want that job for everyone. Whatever we pick has to give the quiet ones real work.
So you'll tell them we're building an escape room?
No, I still don't want our room locked up all day where nobody can just wander in and see us.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Imogen express about the festival options?
choices: Performing on stage builds confidence more than anything else.
Quieter students can contribute a great deal behind the scenes.
Selling food is the fairest way to include everybody.
Visitors prefer events they do not have to book in advance.
q34.heard: the shy ones end up writing puzzles instead of performing
q34.explain: Imogen が escape room を推す理由は「Every single person gets a job, and the shy ones end up writing puzzles instead of performing」→「the quiet members did the best work of anyone」。おとなしい生徒が裏方で活躍できる、で②です。②の英文はそのまま読まれません。
keyPhrases: the shy ones end up writing puzzles instead of performing
the quiet members did the best work of anyone

distractors.why: Imogen は逆に「performing の代わりに puzzles を書く」ことを利点として挙げています。
「みんな手伝える・人前に立たなくていい」は Hugo が food stall を推した理由です。話者の入れ替え。
Imogen は「visitors book slots」で人数が読めることを利点としています。予約なしを好むとは逆方向です。

q35.prompt: Which option did Hugo decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The escape room
The exhibition
The food stall
The stage play

requires.cond: おとなしい生徒にも実際の役割がある形にしたい（escape room の要素）
requires.line: I want that job for everyone. Whatever we pick has to give the quiet ones real work.

requires.cond: それでも誰でもふらっと入って見られる形にしたい
requires.line: No, I still don't want our room locked up all day where nobody can just wander in and see us.

q35.explain: Hugo は「全員に役割を」と言った直後、「escape room を作ると伝える?」に No と答え、「誰でも入って見られるようにしたい」と言います。教室を使い、来場者が自由に歩いて見られて、準備の役割が全員にある exhibition だけが両方を満たします。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: 「building an escape room?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると①になります。
序盤の「I was going to say the food stall」は、おとなしい生徒の話で自ら覆します。
stage play は人前に立つ形で、Hugo が最も避けたい方向です。一度も希望していません。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Zane, Bethan, Nils)が，廊下を走ることについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Zane
speakers.role: student who always runs and finally stops
speakers.tone: energetic, laughs at himself, sincere at the end

speakers.name: Bethan
speakers.role: student who agrees loudly but keeps running
speakers.tone: warm, agrees with everyone, does not notice her own contradiction

speakers.name: Nils
speakers.role: student who read the nurse's records
speakers.tone: steady, unhurried, gives numbers plainly

conversation.text: I nearly took out a first-year outside the staff room this morning. He came round the corner just as I did, and neither of us was going slowly.
That corner is genuinely dangerous. You cannot see anyone coming until you are already on top of them. Somebody should put a mirror up there before somebody gets properly hurt.

The nurse keeps a record of every injury she treats, and I asked her about it last week. Of everyone who came in hurt last term, sixty-eight students were injured in corridor collisions, which was more than any other cause.
Sixty-eight? More than the sports injuries? We have four teams.
Sports came second, at about forty-five, and most of those were on the pitch rather than indoors. Corridors were clearly ahead of everything, and the science lab was much lower than I expected.
That's shocking. Everyone should absolutely slow down in the corridors, that's obvious now.
Everyone including you? You overtook me on the stairs about an hour ago.
That was different, I was late for maths. Obviously I mean everyone else.
I can't say that. It was almost me this morning, and I only missed him because he stopped first, so I'll walk that corridor from now on rather than find out what sixty-eight feels like.
I've walked it since the day I started here, because my brother broke his wrist in a corridor at his own school, so nothing changes on my side.
You're going to be insufferable about this for weeks, aren't you.
He already is. Look at his face.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも廊下を歩くようにしようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。

stances.evidence: so I'll walk that corridor from now on rather than find out what sixty-eight feels like.
stances.why: 走る側だったが、衝突が最多という数字と自分のニアミスで方針が動いた。数える。

stances.evidence: Everyone should absolutely slow down in the corridors, that's obvious now.
stances.why: ★最も大きな声で賛成しているので数えたくなるが、直後に「Obviously I mean everyone else」と自分は除外している。数えない。

stances.evidence: I've walked it since the day I started here, because my brother broke his wrist in a corridor at his own school, so nothing changes on my side.
stances.why: ★入学時からもともと歩いている。「以前よりも」歩くようになる人ではない。数えない。

graphs.measures: けがの原因ごとの生徒の人数

q37.explain: 数字＝68／対象＝保健室で手当を受けた生徒／出来事＝けがの原因。④だけが「原因ごとの人数」を数え、Corridor collisions が 68 で最多、Sports が 45（Nils の「Sports came second, at about forty-five」）とも一致します。①③も68が出ますが、月別の人数と通行人数で別の集計です。

sets.topic: A: 卒業旅行の移動手段／B: 教科書の電子化

partA.situation: Nadine と Rafferty が，卒業旅行の移動手段をどれにするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Nadine
speakers.role: student who has already priced all four options
speakers.tone: confident, slightly teasing, produces numbers from memory

speakers.name: Rafferty
speakers.role: student who has to book tonight and keeps two conditions
speakers.tone: easy-going, thinks aloud, unexpectedly firm at the close

conversation.text: Nadine, the group booking closes at midnight and I still haven't picked how we're getting there. Run the four past me.

The night bus is the cheapest by far and takes eleven hours. The flight is ninety minutes but you lose most of the saving to the airport transfers. The express train is four hours, twice the bus price, with a proper table to sit at. And the rental van is one price split between us, and one of us has to drive the whole way.
I'd been assuming the night bus. It's the cheapest thing on the list and we're all broke after this term.

It's cheap, but count what it actually costs you. Eleven hours upright means you arrive unable to think, and we lose the first day of a four-day trip to everyone sleeping it off. The train got us there before lunch last year.
So the cheap option quietly eats a quarter of the holiday. That's a real number, put like that.
And on the train we can actually sit facing each other and plan the days properly.
Right, I won't book anything that costs us a day at the far end. We have to arrive able to function.
So shall I put all six of us on the express train?
No, we still cannot pay twice the bus fare, and nobody in this group wants to spend the trip driving.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Nadine express about the travel options?
choices: Airport transfers are more tiring than long train journeys.
The cheapest option wastes part of the holiday itself.
Driving themselves would give the group the most freedom.
The group's limited money should decide which option they take.
q34.heard: we lose the first day of a four-day trip
q34.explain: Nadine が night bus を否定する根拠は「Eleven hours upright means you arrive unable to think, and we lose the first day of a four-day trip to everyone sleeping it off」。安い選択が旅行そのものを削る、で②です。②の英文はそのまま読まれません。
keyPhrases: we lose the first day of a four-day trip
The train got us there before lunch last year

distractors.why: airport transfers は「節約分が消える」というお金の話で、疲労の比較はしていません。
rental van は「誰かが全部運転する」と説明しただけで、自由さの利点は誰も述べていません。
「お金で決めるべき」は Rafferty の立場です（we're all broke after this term / we still cannot pay twice the bus fare）。Nadine は逆に「安さだけで決めると旅行の一日を失う」と言っています。話者の入れ替え。

q35.prompt: Which option did Rafferty decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The express train
The flight
The night bus
The rental van

requires.cond: 到着後に1日を潰すような移動は選ばない（＝短時間で着く）
requires.line: I won't book anything that costs us a day at the far end. We have to arrive able to function.

requires.cond: それでもバス運賃の2倍は払えず、誰も運転したくない
requires.line: No, we still cannot pay twice the bus fare, and nobody in this group wants to spend the trip driving.

q35.explain: Rafferty は「1日潰す移動は選ばない」と言った直後、「express train でいい?」に No と答え、2倍の運賃も運転も無理だと言います。90分で着き、train の2倍運賃にも当たらず、運転も不要な flight だけが両方を満たします。どの1発話にも答えは書かれていません。

distractors.why: 「put all six of us on the express train?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると①になります。
序盤の「I'd been assuming the night bus」は、11時間で1日を失うという話で自ら覆します。
最後に「nobody in this group wants to spend the trip driving」と明確に除外しています。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Soraya, Emmet, Ingrid)が，教科書を紙から電子に替えるかについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Soraya
speakers.role: student who dislikes screens but shifts in the end
speakers.tone: sceptical and dry, concedes reluctantly

speakers.name: Emmet
speakers.role: student who also shifts after hearing the figures
speakers.tone: curious, does the arithmetic aloud

speakers.name: Ingrid
speakers.role: student who has used digital books since her first year
speakers.tone: relaxed, quotes the library report without pushing it

conversation.text: My bag weighed about nine kilos this morning and four of those kilos were one economics textbook. My shoulder is making a noise it shouldn't make.
I still prefer paper. I remember where things are on a page, and I can't do that on a screen at all.
I've read everything digitally since first year, so my bag has a laptop in it and nothing else.
Nothing else at all? What about the ones the library doesn't have as files?

That's the part that surprised me. The library published its report last month, and of every title on our reading lists, three hundred and forty are now available as licensed files, which is more than in any other format they hold.
Three hundred and forty? More than the printed copies they keep on the shelves?
Printed copies came second, at about two hundred and ten. Files were well ahead, and the audio versions were far lower.
So the thing I've been carrying in paper is mostly available as a file I already have access to. That's slightly humiliating.
It is. Fine, I'll read the long ones on the tablet from next week rather than carry them across town twice a day.
I'm switching for the heavy ones too, starting with the economics one that's ruining my shoulder.
I'll carry on exactly as I am, which is the nicest sentence in this conversation.
You've been waiting two years to say that, haven't you.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも電子の教科書を使おうと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より電子の教科書を使う

stances.evidence: I'll read the long ones on the tablet from next week rather than carry them across town twice a day.
stances.why: ★「I still prefer paper」と強く言うので数えたくなくなるが、最後に「来週からタブレットで読む」と明言している。数える。

stances.evidence: I'm switching for the heavy ones too, starting with the economics one that's ruining my shoulder.
stances.why: 紙を運んでいたが、340点が電子で使えると知って切り替えると明言。数える。

stances.evidence: I've read everything digitally since first year, so my bag has a laptop in it and nothing else.
stances.why: ★1年次からもともと電子。「以前よりも」使うようになる人ではない。数えない。

q36.explain: 動いたのは Soraya と Emmet の2人＝②。Soraya は序盤に強く紙を擁護するので落としやすいですが、最後に切り替えています。Ingrid はもともと電子なので「以前よりも」に当たりません。3人とも電子に前向きに聞こえるので③にしがちです。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Ingrid の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.utterance: three hundred and forty are now available as licensed files, which is more than in any other format they hold
basis.event: how many titles the library holds in each format

graphs.measures: 形式ごとに図書館が持っているタイトル数

graphs.measures: 年ごとに追加された電子タイトル数
graphs.whyWrong: 340 もタイトル数も合いますが、年ごとの追加数で、形式どうしの比較ではありません。Ingrid は「他のどの形式より多い」と言っています。

graphs.title: Average Weight of Student Bags by Year Group
graphs.measures: 学年ごとのかばんの平均重量
graphs.whyWrong: 測っているのは重さで、タイトル数ではありません。340 という値も出てきません。

graphs.title: How Students Say They Prefer to Read
graphs.measures: 読み方の好みの割合
graphs.whyWrong: 学生の好みの割合で、図書館の所蔵数ではありません。単位も％です。

q37.explain: 数字＝340／対象＝リーディングリストのタイトル／出来事＝形式ごとの所蔵数。①だけが「形式別のタイトル数」を数え、Licensed files が 340 で最多、Printed copies が 210（Ingrid の「Printed copies came second, at about two hundred and ten」）とも一致します。②は340もタイトルも合いますが年別の追加数で、形式を比べていません。

sets.topic: A: アルバイト先の選択／B: 授業中にスマホを机に出さない

partA.situation: Marcus と Hanae が，アルバイト先をどこにするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Marcus
speakers.role: student who has looked into all four jobs and warns about the cost of high pay
speakers.tone: level-headed, uses his brother's experience as evidence

speakers.name: Hanae
speakers.role: student who must answer by Friday and decides at the very end
speakers.tone: attracted by the money at first, then rules options out one by one

conversation.text: Marcus, I have to answer by Friday and I still cannot choose. Go through the four with me again.

The cafe pays eight fifty an hour, shifts finish at ten, and you choose your days. The bookshop pays about the same, but it is whole weekends, Saturday and Sunday, nothing midweek. The tutoring centre pays fourteen, teaching maths to fifteen year olds. And the delivery job pays the most of any of them, because the shifts run from nine until one in the morning.
Fourteen an hour is nearly double the cafe. I had been leaning towards the tutoring centre just for that.

Look at what the money costs you. My brother took the delivery job last year for exactly that reason, and the money is meaningless if you sleep through the lecture you are paying for. He failed two modules and repeated the year.
So a high hourly rate can quietly take away the thing I came here to do.
Exactly. Wages you can earn again later. A repeated year you cannot.
Right. I will not take anything that has me finishing after midnight. That settles at least one of them.
So shall I tell the tutoring centre you are interested? It is the best paid of the three left.
No, and I cannot teach maths to anyone, so that is out as well. And you know I have practice both days at the weekend.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Marcus express about the jobs?
choices: The highest hourly rate should decide the choice.
A job that ruins the next day's study is not worth the higher pay.
Late shifts are acceptable as long as they are well paid.
Work experience matters more than pay at this age.
q34.heard: the money is meaningless if you sleep through the lecture you are paying for
q34.explain: Marcus は delivery job を否定する根拠として「the money is meaningless if you sleep through the lecture you are paying for」「He failed two modules and repeated the year」と言い、さらに「Wages you can earn again later. A repeated year you cannot.」と結びます。高い時給が翌日の学業を壊すなら意味がない、で②です。②の英文は対話にそのままは読まれません。
keyPhrases: the money is meaningless if you sleep through the lecture you are paying for
He failed two modules and repeated the year

distractors.why: 「時給の高さで決める」は序盤の Hanae の立場（Fourteen an hour is nearly double the cafe）です。Marcus はそれを否定しています。話者の入れ替え。
Marcus の主張と正反対です。彼は「よく稼げる深夜シフトだからこそ危ない」と言っています。
work experience（経験）の価値は誰も話題にしていません。Marcus が比べているのは賃金と学業です。

q35.prompt: Which job did Hanae decide to take at the end of the conversation?
choices: The bookshop
The cafe
The delivery job
The tutoring centre

requires.cond: 深夜に終わる仕事はしない（delivery が消える）
requires.line: I will not take anything that has me finishing after midnight.

requires.cond: 数学は教えられない（tutoring centre が消える）
requires.line: I cannot teach maths to anyone, so that is out as well.

requires.cond: 週末は両日とも部活の練習がある（bookshop が消える）
requires.line: you know I have practice both days at the weekend

q35.explain: Hanae は「深夜に終わる仕事はしない」で delivery を、「数学は教えられない」で tutoring centre を、「週末は両日とも練習がある」で whole weekends の bookshop を、それぞれ自分で消します。残るのは cafe だけで②。どの1発話にも「cafe にする」とは言っていません。

distractors.why: bookshop は土日終日で、Hanae は最後に「practice both days at the weekend」と言っています。この一言を聞き落とすと①に見えます。
delivery は最も稼げますが「深夜に終わる仕事はしない」に真っ向から反します。金額だけで選ぶと③になります。
序盤の「I had been leaning towards the tutoring centre」は時給だけを見た希望で、最後に自分で否定します。Marcus の「shall I tell the tutoring centre?」に No と答えている点も決定的です。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Fintan, Marisol, Gwen)が，授業中にスマホを机の上に置かないことについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Fintan
speakers.role: student who witnessed the lecturer stop and who moves first
speakers.tone: wry, tells the story with amusement, then commits plainly

speakers.name: Marisol
speakers.role: student who resists loudly and gives in only at the very end
speakers.tone: defensive, argumentative, dislikes being told what to do

speakers.name: Gwen
speakers.role: student who read the department survey and quotes the figures
speakers.tone: calm, precise, admits at the end that she is no better

conversation.text: Doctor Hale stopped mid-sentence today and simply looked at the back row. Four phones face up on the desks, and every one of them lit up while she stood there waiting.
Mine was one of the four and I will not pretend otherwise. It stays on the desk because I want to know at once if somebody needs me.

The department ran a survey about exactly this last term. Of all the students who admitted checking their phone in class, two hundred and sixty said they did it because a notification had appeared on the screen, which was more than any other reason.
So it is not that people want to look. The screen asks them to, and they answer it.
Boredom came second, at about a hundred and seventy five. Family messages were much lower, and hardly anybody said they were checking the time.
Two hundred and sixty out of how many, though? That number means nothing on its own.
Out of six hundred who answered. So nearly half the year group loses the thread of a lecture because a screen flashed at them.
That is me, then. I will put mine in my bag from Monday rather than let a notification decide when I stop listening.
You are both looking at me now, and I can feel it.
I am in no position to look at anybody. Mine has been face down beside my pen for this entire conversation, so I will start doing the thing I am telling everyone else to do.
Fine. Not because either of you asked me, but because I do not like being one of two hundred and sixty. It goes in the bag.
Witnessed, and I am telling Doctor Hale on Monday.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも授業中にスマホをかばんに入れておこうと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より授業中にスマホをかばんに入れておく

stances.evidence: I will put mine in my bag from Monday rather than let a notification decide when I stop listening.
stances.why: 自分も机に出していた側だが、通知が原因という数字を聞いて月曜からかばんに入れると明言。数える。

stances.evidence: Fine. Not because either of you asked me, but because I do not like being one of two hundred and sixty. It goes in the bag.
stances.why: ★最後まで反発した言い方をするので数えたくなくなるが、「It goes in the bag」と明確に行動を変えている。渋る口調にだまされない。数える。

stances.evidence: Mine has been face down beside my pen for this entire conversation, so I will start doing the thing I am telling everyone else to do.
stances.why: ★数字を出す側なのでもともとやっていると思い込みやすいが、本人が「会話中ずっと机に置いていた」と認め、これから変えると言っている。数える。

q36.explain: 3人全員が動いたので③。Marisol は最後まで反発した言い方をしますが「It goes in the bag」と行動を変えており、口調で判断すると②に落ちます。Gwen は数字を出す側なのでもともと守っていると思い込みがちですが、本人が机に置いていたと認めているので、これも数えます。
q36.trapNote: ①②に見せる罠が2つ。Marisol の渋る口調と、Gwen が「注意する側だからもともとやっている」という思い込み。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Gwen の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.utterance: two hundred and sixty said they did it because a notification had appeared on the screen, which was more than any other reason
basis.target: students who check their phone in class

graphs.title: Phones Seen Face Up on Desks by Month
graphs.measures: 月ごとに机の上で見られたスマホの台数
graphs.whyWrong: 260 もスマホの話も合いますが、数えているのは月ごとの推移で、理由の比較ではありません。Gwen は「どの理由より多かった」と言っています。

graphs.title: Reasons Students Check Their Phone in Class
graphs.measures: 授業中にスマホを見た理由ごとの学生数

graphs.title: Where Students Keep Their Phone During Class
graphs.measures: 授業中にスマホをどこに置いているかの割合
graphs.whyWrong: 置き場所の割合で、見た理由の集計ではありません。260 という値も出てきません。

graphs.title: Notifications Received per Day by App Type
graphs.measures: アプリの種類ごとに1日に届く通知の件数
graphs.whyWrong: 数えているのは通知の件数で、学生の人数ではありません。notification という語につられると④を選んでしまいます。

q37.explain: 数字＝260／対象＝授業中にスマホを見た学生／出来事＝その理由。②だけが「理由ごとの学生数」を数え、Notification が 260 で最多、Boredom が 175（Gwen の「Boredom came second, at about a hundred and seventy five」）とも一致します。①は260もスマホも合いますが月別推移です。④は notification という語が目に入りますが、数えているのは通知件数で人数ではありません。

sets.topic: A: 遠足の行き先／B: 図書館で飲み物を持ち込まない

partA.situation: Duncan と Miyu が，クラスの遠足の行き先をどこにするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Duncan
speakers.role: student who has checked all four destinations and worries about the travelling time
speakers.tone: friendly, gives the details clearly, easy to follow

speakers.name: Miyu
speakers.role: class representative who has to report the choice tomorrow
speakers.tone: cheerful, keen on the aquarium at first, decides at the very end

conversation.text: Duncan, I have to report our choice to the teacher tomorrow morning. Tell me about the four places again.

The science museum is forty minutes away by bus and free for schools. The aquarium is two and a half hours each way, and the tickets are twelve pounds each. The castle is an hour away, five pounds, and there is a guided tour. And the botanical garden is twenty minutes on foot from school, free, but it is entirely outdoors.
Everybody keeps saying the aquarium. It is the one place none of us has been to.

Think about the timetable, though. Five hours on a bus out of a seven hour day means we would see the tanks for less than two hours. We would spend the day travelling to a place instead of being at it.
So the most exciting place gives us the least time there. I had not done that arithmetic.
And on a short journey we arrive awake and we can stay until the afternoon.
All right. I will not choose anywhere that takes more than an hour to reach. That rules the aquarium out.
So shall I write down the botanical garden? It is the closest of the three that are left.
No, the forecast is rain all week, and Mr Ito said the trip has to be free this year.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Duncan express about the destinations?
choices: The cheapest destination is usually the best one.
A guided tour makes a trip more valuable.
A long journey takes away the time you have at the place itself.
Outdoor trips are better than indoor ones.
q34.heard: We would spend the day travelling to a place instead of being at it
q34.explain: Duncan が aquarium を止める根拠は「Five hours on a bus out of a seven hour day means we would see the tanks for less than two hours」「We would spend the day travelling to a place instead of being at it」。長い移動が現地での時間を奪う、で③です。③の英文は対話にそのままは読まれません。
keyPhrases: We would spend the day travelling to a place instead of being at it
we arrive awake and we can stay until the afternoon

distractors.why: Duncan が問題にしているのは値段ではなく移動時間です。usually the best one という一般化も強すぎます。
guided tour は castle の説明として一度出るだけで、その価値を Duncan は論じていません。
屋外か屋内かを気にしているのは最後の Miyu（the forecast is rain all week）です。話者の入れ替え。

q35.prompt: Which destination did Miyu decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The aquarium
The botanical garden
The castle
The science museum

requires.cond: 片道1時間を超える場所は選ばない（aquarium が消える）
requires.line: I will not choose anywhere that takes more than an hour to reach.

requires.cond: 一週間ずっと雨の予報なので屋外は避ける（botanical garden が消える）
requires.line: the forecast is rain all week

requires.cond: 今年の遠足は無料でなければならない（castle が消える）
requires.line: Mr Ito said the trip has to be free this year

q35.explain: Miyu は「1時間超は選ばない」で aquarium を、「一週間雨」で屋外の botanical garden を、「無料でなければならない」で5ポンドの castle を消します。40分・無料・屋内の science museum だけが残り④。どの1発話にも「science museum にする」とは言っていません。

distractors.why: 序盤の「Everybody keeps saying the aquarium」は希望で、直後に自分で「1時間超は選ばない」と否定します。
Duncan の「shall I write down the botanical garden?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると②になります。
castle は1時間で条件を満たしますが5ポンドかかります。「has to be free」を聞き落とすと③に見えます。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Aled, Junko, Rune)が，図書館に飲み物を持ち込まないことについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Aled
speakers.role: student who agrees with everything but exempts himself
speakers.tone: enthusiastic agreement, then a quiet excuse

speakers.name: Junko
speakers.role: student who sets a condition that the library will never meet
speakers.tone: polite, sounds cooperative, always has one more requirement

speakers.name: Rune
speakers.role: student who found the librarian's record and has never brought a drink in
speakers.tone: matter-of-fact, reads the numbers, slightly smug

conversation.text: Somebody spilled orange juice across the reference shelf on Tuesday. Three books are drying on the radiator and one of them is not going to recover.
That is awful. Nobody should be taking drinks in there at all, honestly. It should be a rule and the librarian should say so.
She keeps a record of every damaged book. Of all the books she had to withdraw last year, ninety two were damaged by spilled drinks, which was more than any other cause.
Ninety two books? From drinks alone?
Torn pages came second, at about fifty five. Water from bags was much lower, and only a handful were damaged by sunlight.
That does change how it looks. I will leave my tea outside the day they put a shelf by the door for it.
There is a shelf by the door already. It has been there since September.
For umbrellas. I am not putting a cup of tea where wet umbrellas go, so my offer stands as it is.
And you, Aled? You said nobody should take drinks in there.
Nobody should. I mean, mine is a sealed bottle with a screw top, so it cannot spill, so obviously I meant everybody else.
I have never taken anything in there since first year, so nothing changes on my side either.
Then the three of us have achieved absolutely nothing this lunchtime.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも図書館に飲み物を持ち込まないようにしようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より図書館に飲み物を持ち込まない

stances.evidence: Nobody should be taking drinks in there at all, honestly.
stances.why: ★最も強く賛成しているので数えたくなるが、最後に「mine is a sealed bottle ... so obviously I meant everybody else」と自分を除外している。数えない。

stances.evidence: I will leave my tea outside the day they put a shelf by the door for it.
stances.why: ★「やる」と言うので数えたくなるが、条件は「お茶用の棚を置いたら」で、既にある棚は傘用だと本人が拒否し「my offer stands as it is」と言う。条件は満たされない。数えない。

stances.why: ★1年次から一度も持ち込んでいない。「以前よりも」持ち込まなくなる人ではない。数えない。

q36.explain: 動いた人は1人もいないので④＝0人。Aled は最も強く賛成しますが自分だけ例外にし、Junko は条件を出しますがその条件は満たされず、Rune はもともと持ち込んでいません。3人とも前向きに聞こえるので③、Aled と Junko を拾うと②に見えるのが罠です。最後の Junko の「the three of us have achieved absolutely nothing」が答え合わせになります。
q36.trapNote: 3人全員に別の型の罠。前向きな言葉だけを数えると③、二人を拾うと②。0人という選択肢を最初から視野に入れているかが問われる。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Rune の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.utterance: ninety two were damaged by spilled drinks, which was more than any other cause
basis.target: library books withdrawn because of damage

graphs.title: Books Withdrawn Each Year

graphs.whyWrong: 92 も廃棄本も合いますが、年ごとの推移で、原因の比較ではありません。Rune は「どの原因より多かった」と言っています。

graphs.measures: 図書館で飲まれている飲み物の割合

sets.topic: A: 研究発表に使う資料の形式／B: 実験室で私語をやめる

partA.situation: Dr Whitlock と Theo が，研究発表で配る資料をどの形式にするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Dr Whitlock
speakers.role: supervisor who has seen all four formats fail or succeed at conferences
speakers.tone: dry, precise, argues from what the audience actually does

speakers.name: Theo
speakers.role: graduate student who must send the file to the printer tonight
speakers.tone: eager, wants the most impressive option, concedes reluctantly

conversation.text: Doctor Whitlock, the printer needs the file tonight. Could you go over the four formats once more?

A single page summary costs nothing and fits in a pocket. The twelve page booklet holds every table you have, but it is forty pounds for the run. A QR code on the slide costs nothing and sends them to the full data online. And the poster is striking, but there is only one of it, so nobody takes anything away.
I had been planning the booklet. It shows how much work went into this, and nothing gets left out.
Consider what people actually do with twelve pages. They put it in a bag at the first session and it is never opened again. What travels is the thing they can read while they walk to the next room.
So including everything is the same as including nothing, if it never gets read.
Precisely. And a summary they read in a corridor is worth more than a booklet in a drawer.
All right. I will not print anything that people have to sit down to read. It has to work on its feet.
So shall I approve the QR code? It costs nothing and it carries every table you have.
No, half the rooms in that building have no signal at all, and I need something each person can carry out with them.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Dr Whitlock express about the handout formats?
choices: The cost of printing should be the main consideration.
Every table in the study should be included in the handout.
A handout is only worth making if the audience will actually read it.
A striking visual is what an audience remembers.
q34.heard: They put it in a bag at the first session and it is never opened again
q34.explain: Dr Whitlock が booklet を否定する根拠は「They put it in a bag at the first session and it is never opened again」「a summary they read in a corridor is worth more than a booklet in a drawer」。読まれないなら作る意味がない、で③です。③の英文は対話にそのままは読まれません。
keyPhrases: They put it in a bag at the first session and it is never opened again
a summary they read in a corridor is worth more than a booklet in a drawer

distractors.why: 40ポンドという金額は形式の説明として述べただけで、Dr Whitlock は費用を判断基準にしていません。
「全部載せる」は序盤の Theo の立場（nothing gets left out）です。Dr Whitlock はそれを「読まれなければ同じ」と否定しています。話者の入れ替え。
poster を striking と説明はしましたが、直後に「nobody takes anything away」と欠点を挙げています。印象に残るから良いとは言っていません。

q35.prompt: Which format did Theo decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The one page summary
The poster
The QR code on the slide
The twelve page booklet

requires.cond: 座って読まなければならないものは印刷しない（booklet が消える）
requires.line: I will not print anything that people have to sit down to read.

requires.cond: 会場の半分は電波が入らない（QR code が消える）
requires.line: half the rooms in that building have no signal at all

requires.cond: 一人ひとりが持ち帰れるものが必要（poster が消える）
requires.line: I need something each person can carry out with them

q35.explain: Theo は「座って読むものは印刷しない」で booklet を、「半分の部屋は電波が入らない」で QR code を、「各人が持ち帰れるものが必要」で1枚しかない poster を消します。残るのは one page summary だけで①。どの1発話にも「summary にする」とは言っていません。

distractors.why: poster は座って読む必要も電波も不要ですが「一人ひとりが持ち帰れる」を満たしません。最後の条件を聞き落とすと②に見えます。
Dr Whitlock の「shall I approve the QR code?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると③になります。
序盤の「I had been planning the booklet」は希望で、自分で「座って読むものは印刷しない」と覆します。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Oskar, Priya, Callista)が，実験室での私語をやめることについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Oskar
speakers.role: student who caused a spoiled experiment and changes first
speakers.tone: embarrassed, honest, does not make excuses

speakers.name: Priya
speakers.role: student who protests all the way through but changes at the end
speakers.tone: combative, sharp questions, concedes only on her own terms

speakers.name: Callista
speakers.role: student who pulled the technician's log and also admits she talks
speakers.tone: measured, reads figures off a printout, self-critical at the end

conversation.text: I ruined a titration yesterday. Priya asked me a question, I answered, and I put in five drops too many while I was talking.
That is not on me. You could have said you were counting. Talking in a lab is normal, it is how anyone learns anything.

The technician logs every spoiled sample. Of all the samples that had to be discarded last term, one hundred and forty were spoiled by a counting or timing mistake, which was more than any other reason.
So the commonest way to lose a sample is to lose your place in a count.
Wrong reagent came second, at about eighty five. Contamination was lower again, and equipment faults were rare.
One hundred and forty out of how many samples in total? Without that this figure tells us nothing.
Out of three hundred and ten. So nearly half of everything discarded went because somebody lost count.
That settles it for me. I will keep quiet while I am counting from now on, rather than throw away another afternoon.
I still think a silent lab is a worse place to learn in.
I am not innocent here either. I talk through every single titration I do, so I should be the second person to stop, not the one lecturing about it.
Then I will hold my questions until the counting stops. Not because you two have shamed me into it, but because forty five wasted samples a term is genuinely absurd.
That is the most gracious surrender I have ever heard.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも実験室で私語を控えようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より実験室で私語を控える

stances.evidence: I will keep quiet while I am counting from now on, rather than throw away another afternoon.
stances.why: 自分の失敗と140という数字を受けて、これからは数えている間は黙ると明言。数える。

stances.evidence: Then I will hold my questions until the counting stops.
stances.why: ★直前に「I still think a silent lab is a worse place to learn in」と反対の意見を言うので数えたくなくなるが、最後に「質問は数え終わるまで待つ」と行動を変えている。意見と行動を分けて聞く。数える。

stances.evidence: I talk through every single titration I do, so I should be the second person to stop, not the one lecturing about it.
stances.why: ★データを出す側なのでもともと静かにしていると思い込みやすいが、本人が「毎回しゃべり通している」と認め、自分も止めると言っている。数える。

q36.explain: 3人全員が動いたので③。Priya は最後まで「静かな実験室のほうが学びにくい」という意見を保ったままですが、行動としては「数え終わるまで質問を待つ」と変えています。意見が変わっていないことと行動が変わったことを混同すると②になります。Callista は注意する側ですが、自分もしゃべっていたと認めているので数えます。
q36.trapNote: 意見は変えないが行動は変える Priya と、注意する側だから元から守っていると思わせる Callista。両方を取りこぼすと①になる。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Callista の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.utterance: one hundred and forty were spoiled by a counting or timing mistake, which was more than any other reason

graphs.title: Samples Discarded Each Term
graphs.measures: 学期ごとに廃棄されたサンプル数
graphs.whyWrong: 140 も廃棄サンプルも合いますが、学期ごとの推移で、理由の比較ではありません。Callista は「どの理由より多かった」と言っています。

graphs.title: Reasons Samples Were Discarded
graphs.measures: 廃棄された理由ごとのサンプル数

graphs.title: Time Spent Talking During Laboratory Sessions
graphs.measures: 学年ごとに実験中に会話している時間
graphs.whyWrong: 数えているのは会話の時間で、サンプル数ではありません。私語という話題が同じだけです。

graphs.title: Who Discards the Most Samples
graphs.measures: 廃棄サンプルを出した学生の学年の割合
graphs.whyWrong: 廃棄した学生の学年の割合で、理由の集計ではありません。140 という値も出てきません。

q37.explain: 数字＝140／対象＝廃棄されたサンプル／出来事＝廃棄の理由。②だけが「理由ごとのサンプル数」を数え、Counting が 140 で最多、Wrong reagent が 85（Callista の「Wrong reagent came second, at about eighty five」）とも一致します。①は140も廃棄サンプルも合いますが学期別推移です。

sets.topic: A: 部活のユニフォームの注文先／B: 体育館シューズを履き替える

partA.situation: Imani と Reo が，部活の新しいユニフォームをどこに注文するかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Imani
speakers.role: deputy captain who has quotes from all four suppliers
speakers.tone: organised, warns about delivery dates, quotes numbers unprompted

speakers.name: Reo
speakers.role: captain who must place the order this evening
speakers.tone: drawn to the cheapest quote, then rules options out one at a time

conversation.text: Imani, I have to place the order this evening. Run the four suppliers past me one last time.

The online factory is by far the cheapest, but delivery is eight to ten weeks. The shop in town is the most expensive and can have them ready in five days. The sports club supplier is in the middle and takes three weeks. And the parents' committee offered to sew them, free, but only two of them can actually sew.
The online factory, surely. It is half the price of anything else on that list.

Look at the date, though. Ten weeks puts them here after the regional tournament, so we would pay for shirts nobody wears in the one match that matters. Cheap kit that arrives late is money we simply threw away.
So the saving disappears if we cannot wear them when it counts.
And arriving in matching kit is half of what makes the team look like a team on that day.
Fine. I will not order anything that arrives after the tournament. That has to be the first condition.
So shall I ring the shop in town? Five days is the safest of anything on the list.
No, we cannot pay their price out of what is left, and I am not asking two parents to sew nineteen shirts.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Imani express about the suppliers?
choices: Handmade kit means more to a team than bought kit.
Local suppliers are more reliable than distant ones.
A low price is wasted if the kit arrives too late to be used.
The team should spend as much as it can afford on kit.
q34.heard: Cheap kit that arrives late is money we simply threw away
q34.explain: Imani が online factory を止める根拠は「Ten weeks puts them here after the regional tournament, so we would pay for shirts nobody wears in the one match that matters」「Cheap kit that arrives late is money we simply threw away」。安さは間に合わなければ無駄、で③です。③の英文は対話にそのままは読まれません。
keyPhrases: Cheap kit that arrives late is money we simply threw away
we would pay for shirts nobody wears in the one match that matters

distractors.why: 手作りに触れたのは供給元の説明としてで、しかも「two of them can actually sew」と限界を指摘しています。手作りに価値があるとは誰も主張していません。
距離と信頼性の関係は誰も述べていません。Imani が問題にしているのは納期です。
Imani の主張と逆方向です。彼女は高く買えとは言っておらず、最後に Reo が予算の限界を述べています。

q35.prompt: Which supplier did Reo decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The online factory
The parents' committee
The shop in town
The sports club supplier

requires.cond: 大会の後に届くものは注文しない（online factory が消える）
requires.line: I will not order anything that arrives after the tournament.

requires.cond: 残った予算では町の店の価格は払えない（shop in town が消える）
requires.line: we cannot pay their price out of what is left

requires.cond: 2人の保護者に19枚を縫わせるのは無理（parents' committee が消える）
requires.line: I am not asking two parents to sew nineteen shirts

q35.explain: Reo は「大会の後に届くものは注文しない」で online factory を、「その価格は払えない」で shop in town を、「2人に19枚は無理」で parents' committee を消します。3週間・中間価格の sports club supplier だけが残り④。どの1発話にも「sports club supplier にする」とは言っていません。

distractors.why: 序盤の「The online factory, surely」は値段だけを見た希望で、自分で「大会後に届くものは注文しない」と覆します。
無料で納期も早そうに聞こえますが、Reo が最後に「2人の保護者に19枚は頼まない」と自分で消しています。
Imani の「shall I ring the shop in town?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると③になります。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Bram, Saki, Colm)が，体育館に入るときに靴を履き替えることについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Bram
speakers.role: student who agrees loudly but exempts his own trainers
speakers.tone: hearty, indignant on behalf of others, quietly self-serving

speakers.name: Saki
speakers.role: student who sets a condition the school will not meet
speakers.tone: reasonable in tone, immovable in practice

speakers.name: Colm
speakers.role: student who has the caretaker's repair figures and has always changed shoes
speakers.tone: unhurried, reads from a note, unbothered by the others

conversation.text: The caretaker has taped off the corner under the north basket again. That is the third patch of floor he has lost this year to marks he cannot get out.
That is ridiculous. Everyone should be changing their shoes at the door, it takes about nine seconds. The teachers should be checking it properly.
He keeps a note of every repair he books. Of all the floor repairs in the gym last year, seventy eight were caused by outdoor shoes, which was more than any other cause.
Seventy eight repairs from shoes alone? That seems very high.
Dropped equipment came second, at about forty. Water damage was much lower, and only a few were caused by moving the seating.
That is worth knowing. I will change mine the day they put a bench by the gym door to sit on.
There is a bench there. It has been outside that door since before we started here.
That one faces the car park and it is always wet. I am not sitting on that, so my position has not changed.
You cannot argue with seventy eight, though, Saki. That is a lot of floor.
And your own shoes, Bram? You walked in on those this morning.
Mine are indoor trainers that I happen to wear outside, so they are not really outdoor shoes. Obviously I meant everybody else.
I have changed mine at that door since the first week of first year, so nothing is different for me.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも体育館で靴を履き替えようと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より体育館で靴を履き替える

stances.evidence: Everyone should be changing their shoes at the door, it takes about nine seconds.
stances.why: ★最も強く賛成し、Saki まで説得しようとするので数えたくなるが、最後に「Mine are indoor trainers that I happen to wear outside ... Obviously I meant everybody else」と自分を外している。数えない。

stances.evidence: I will change mine the day they put a bench by the gym door to sit on.
stances.why: ★「やる」と言うので数えたくなるが、条件はベンチの設置で、既にあると指摘されると濡れているからと拒否し「my position has not changed」と言う。条件は満たされない。数えない。

stances.evidence: I have changed mine at that door since the first week of first year, so nothing is different for me.
stances.why: ★1年の最初の週からもともと履き替えている。「以前よりも」履き替えるようになる人ではない。数えない。

q36.explain: 動いた人は1人もいないので④＝0人。Bram は最も強く賛成し他人を説得までしますが自分は例外扱い、Saki は条件を出しますが満たされず、Colm はもともと履き替えています。賛成の声だけを数えると③、Bram と Saki を拾うと②に見えるのが罠です。

q37.prompt: 会話を踏まえて，Colm の発言の根拠となる図表を，四つの選択肢(①〜④)のうちから一つ選びなさい。

basis.target: floor repairs booked in the gym

graphs.title: Gym Floor Repairs by Year
graphs.measures: 年ごとの床の修理件数
graphs.whyWrong: 78 も床の修理も合いますが、年ごとの推移で、原因の比較ではありません。Colm は「どの原因より多かった」と言っています。

graphs.title: What Students Wear in the Gym
graphs.measures: 体育館で履いている物の割合
graphs.whyWrong: 履いている物の割合で、修理件数ではありません。78 という値も出てきません。

graphs.title: Causes of Gym Floor Repairs Last Year

graphs.title: Seconds Needed to Change Shoes

sets.topic: A: 誕生日プレゼントの選択／B: 買い物袋を持って行く

partA.situation: Erin と Kaito が，友人の誕生日プレゼントを何にするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Erin
speakers.role: friend who has looked at all four presents and thinks about what will be used
speakers.tone: warm, practical, gives the prices without being asked

speakers.name: Kaito
speakers.role: friend who has to buy the present after school today
speakers.tone: excited about the flashiest option, then narrows it down

conversation.text: Erin, I have to buy it after school today. Go through the four ideas with me one more time.

The headphones are thirty five pounds and the nicest thing on the list. The notebook is six pounds and she writes every single day. The plant is eight pounds, and she has said before that she kills every plant she owns. And the concert ticket is twenty pounds, but it is on the night of her cousin's wedding.
The headphones, obviously. They are the best present of the four by a long way.
She already has headphones, though. Her brother gave her a pair at Christmas and she wears them everywhere. A present she cannot use twice is just a nice object sitting in a drawer.
So the most expensive one might be the one she needs least. That is a strange thought.
And something she reaches for every day reminds her of you every day.
All right. I will not buy her a second one of something she already owns. That is out.
So shall we get the concert ticket? Twenty pounds is well inside your budget.
No, she cannot go that night, and I am not buying a plant for someone who kills them.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Erin express about the presents?
choices: Cheap presents show less thought than expensive ones.
Music is the safest kind of present for a friend.
A present she uses every day is worth more than an expensive one.
A present should be something she has never owned before.
q34.heard: something she reaches for every day reminds her of you every day
q34.explain: Erin が headphones を止める根拠は「A present she cannot use twice is just a nice object sitting in a drawer」で、続けて「something she reaches for every day reminds her of you every day」と言います。毎日使うものの方が価値がある、で③です。③の英文は対話にそのままは読まれません。
keyPhrases: something she reaches for every day reminds her of you every day
A present she cannot use twice is just a nice object sitting in a drawer

distractors.why: Erin の主張と正反対です。彼女は6ポンドの notebook を勧める側です。
音楽関係を推していたのは序盤の Kaito（The headphones, obviously）です。話者の入れ替え。
Erin は「同じものを2つ目は使えない」と言っただけで、「持ったことがないもの」という条件は述べていません。plant も未所有ですが勧めていません。

q35.prompt: Which present did Kaito decide to buy at the end of the conversation?
choices: The concert ticket
The headphones
The notebook
The plant

requires.cond: すでに持っているものの2つ目は買わない（headphones が消える）
requires.line: I will not buy her a second one of something she already owns.

requires.cond: その夜は行けない（concert ticket が消える）
requires.line: she cannot go that night

conversation.text: The recycling room by the halls was full of plastic bags again on Sunday. The bin was so full that the door would not shut properly.

partA.situation: Professor Aldridge と Nadia が，書き上げた論文をどこに出すかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Professor Aldridge
speakers.role: co-author who has published in all four venues and thinks about who will read it

speakers.name: Nadia

conversation.text: Professor Aldridge, the funding report is due in March. Could you take me through the four venues again?

The international journal is the most respected of the four, and review takes fourteen months. The regional conference reviews in six weeks but only fifty people attend. The open access journal reviews in four months and charges a fee of nine hundred pounds. And the departmental working paper series is instant, free, and nobody outside this building reads it.
The international journal, surely. It is the only name on that list anyone would recognise.

Think about what happens in those fourteen months. Two other groups are working on this, and a finding that appears after somebody else has published it is a finding nobody needed. Prestige you can chase again next time. Being first you cannot.
So the most respected route could turn our result into a footnote to someone else's.
And a paper read this spring changes what people do. One read in two years changes nothing at all.
All right. I will not send it anywhere that takes more than six months to review. That is fixed.
So shall I put us down for the open access journal? Four months is comfortably inside your limit.
No, the grant will not cover a nine hundred pound fee, and I need this seen by people outside this department.

That is genuinely wasteful. Nobody should be printing agendas at all any more, everyone has a phone in front of them. Every committee ought to be told.

sets.topic: A: 週末に行う勉強会の場所／B: 自転車を決められた場所に停める

partA.situation: Sinead と Haruki が，週末の勉強会をどこで開くかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Sinead
speakers.role: student who has tried all four places and judges them by how much work gets done

speakers.name: Haruki
speakers.role: student who has to message the group tonight

conversation.text: Sinead, I have to message the group tonight. Take me through the four places one more time.

The cafe on Bridge Street is comfortable and warm, and you cannot hear yourself think after eleven. The library study room is silent and free, but you have to book it fourteen days ahead. My flat is free and available any time, and my brother practises drums on Saturdays. And the community hall is quiet and cheap at five pounds an hour, though it is a forty minute bus ride out of town.
The cafe, obviously. Nobody wants to spend Saturday in a bare room with no coffee.

We tried the cafe in October and we did forty minutes of work in three hours. A place where you cannot finish a sentence is not a place you studied in, it is a place you sat in. Comfort is not the same as getting anything done.
So the nicest room can be the one where the least happens. I had not separated those two things.
And a quiet room on a Saturday morning is worth three noisy afternoons.
Fine. I will not choose anywhere we cannot hold a conversation in. That is the first condition.
So shall I book the library study room? It is silent and it costs nothing at all.
No, this is for the weekend and fourteen days is far too late, and nobody is studying through your brother's drums.

conversation.text: Security cut my lock on Monday and moved my bike to the far compound. I had left it against the fire door by the science block for about twenty minutes.
