sets.topic: A: ボランティア活動の選択／B: 部室の鍵を毎回返す

partA.situation: Rosalind と Yusuf が，夏休みに参加するボランティア活動をどれにするかについて話をしています。

speakers.name: Rosalind
speakers.role: coordinator who has run all four placements and judges them by what the group gains
speakers.tone: warm but frank, uses last year's outcome as evidence

speakers.name: Yusuf
speakers.role: student who must sign up before the deadline on Friday
speakers.tone: drawn to the most impressive placement, then rules them out himself

conversation.text: Rosalind, sign-up closes on Friday. Could you go through the four placements again?

The overseas building project is three weeks abroad and costs eleven hundred pounds in flights. The city food bank is two afternoons a week for the whole summer, and it is ten minutes from here. The beach clean is a single Saturday in August. And the hospital reading scheme takes six weeks of training before you may start.
The overseas project, surely. That is the one that actually looks like something on an application.

Last year's group came back after three weeks and the wall they built was taken down and rebuilt by local bricklayers in two days. Something that ends the moment you fly home has helped you far more than it helped anybody there.
So the placement that looks the most impressive may leave the least behind.
And a group that turns up every week becomes part of how a place runs.
All right. I will not sign up for anything that finishes the day I leave. It has to still be there afterwards.
So shall I put you on the hospital reading scheme? That one certainly continues after you finish.
No, six weeks of training uses up the whole holiday before I start, and one Saturday is over as soon as the tide comes in.

q34.prompt: Which opinion did Rosalind express about the placements?
choices: A placement is only worth doing if it lasts the whole summer.
Training should always come before any volunteering begins.
Volunteering abroad teaches more than volunteering at home.
Work that leaves nothing behind mainly benefits the volunteer.
q34.heard: Something that ends the moment you fly home has helped you far more than it helped anybody there
q34.explain: Rosalind が overseas project を止める根拠は「the wall they built was taken down and rebuilt by local bricklayers in two days」「Something that ends the moment you fly home has helped you far more than it helped anybody there」。後に残らない活動は結局本人のためでしかない、で④です。④の英文は対話にそのままは読まれません。
keyPhrases: Something that ends the moment you fly home has helped you far more than it helped anybody there
a group that turns up every week becomes part of how a place runs

distractors.why: Rosalind は「毎週来る」ことの価値は述べましたが、夏じゅう続くことを条件にはしていません。only worth doing という言い切りが強すぎます。
6週間の研修は hospital reading scheme の説明として述べただけで、研修の必要性を Rosalind は論じていません。研修に触れるのは最後の Yusuf です。
海外を高く評価しているのは序盤の Yusuf（The overseas project, surely）です。Rosalind はそれを否定しています。話者の入れ替え。

q35.prompt: Which placement did Yusuf decide on at the end of the conversation?
choices: The beach clean
The city food bank
The hospital reading scheme
The overseas building project

requires.cond: 自分が去った日に終わるものには申し込まない（overseas project が消える）
requires.line: I will not sign up for anything that finishes the day I leave.

requires.cond: 6週間の研修では休みが終わってしまう（hospital reading scheme が消える）

q35.explain: Yusuf は「自分が去った日に終わるものは申し込まない」で overseas project を、「6週間の研修で休みが終わる」で hospital reading scheme を、「1日で終わる」で beach clean を消します。夏じゅう週2回続く city food bank だけが残り②。どの1発話にも「food bank にする」とは言っていません。

distractors.why: beach clean は費用も研修もかかりませんが、Yusuf 自身が最後に「潮が満ちれば終わる」と消しています。
Rosalind の「shall I put you on the hospital reading scheme?」に No と答えています。ここで Yes と聞き違えると③になります。
序盤の「The overseas project, surely」は見栄えだけを見た希望で、自分で「去った日に終わるものは申し込まない」と覆します。

partB.situation: 三人の学生(Tadhg, Beatriz, Wren)が，部室の鍵を毎回事務室に返すことについて話をしています。

memoTable.lead: 後の表にメモを取ってもかまいません。

speakers.name: Tadhg
speakers.role: student who kept a key in his bag for a fortnight and changes once he hears the count
speakers.tone: sheepish, does not defend himself for long

speakers.name: Beatriz
speakers.role: student who says the office should change instead and never moves herself
speakers.tone: confident, argues the system is at fault, agrees in principle only

speakers.name: Wren
speakers.role: student who got the office's replacement figures and admits she keeps one too
speakers.tone: even, reads the numbers, turns the criticism on herself

conversation.text: The office has changed the lock on the music room again. That is the second new lock this year and the societies are being charged for it.
I had the drama room key in my bag for a fortnight last month. I kept meaning to hand it in and I kept forgetting it was in there.

The office records why each lock has to be replaced. Of all the locks changed on this campus last year, sixty four were changed because a key was never returned, which was more than for any other reason.
Sixty four locks? That is an enormous amount of money for a small thing.
Broken keys came second, at about thirty. Locks damaged by force were lower, and only a few were simply worn out.
So most of that money went on people like me putting a key in a bag and forgetting about it.
The office should put a return box on the corridor wall. Everyone agrees the rule is right, the system around it is just badly designed.
They will not, because the box would have to be emptied by somebody and nobody is paid to do it.
Then the design stays broken and I will keep saying so. I am certainly not queueing at that window every evening.
I will just hand mine in on the way out from now on rather than cost the society another lock.
And I have the darkroom key in my coat at this moment, so I am going to start returning mine as well instead of quoting numbers at everyone.
You two go ahead. I will be here arguing with the office about the box.

q36.questionJa: 会話が終わった時点で、以前よりも部室の鍵を毎回返そうと思っているのは3人のうち何人ですか。
q36.action: 以前より部室の鍵を毎回返す

stances.evidence: I will just hand mine in on the way out from now on rather than cost the society another lock.
stances.why: 2週間持ち帰っていたが、64件という数字を受けてこれからは帰りに返すと明言。数える。

stances.evidence: Everyone agrees the rule is right, the system around it is just badly designed.
stances.why: ★「規則は正しい」と同意し、金額にも驚くので数えたくなるが、変わるべきは事務室の側だという立場を崩さず「I am certainly not queueing at that window every evening」と自分の行動は明確に否定している。数えない。

stances.evidence: I have the darkroom key in my coat at this moment, so I am going to start returning mine as well instead of quoting numbers at everyone.
stances.why: ★数字を出す側なのでもともと返していると思い込みやすいが、本人が「今この瞬間もコートに鍵がある」と認め、これから返すと言っている。数える。

q36.explain: 動いたのは Tadhg と Wren の2人で②。Beatriz は「規則は正しい」と同意し金額にも驚きますが、変わるべきは事務室だという立場のまま「毎晩あの窓口に並ぶ気はない」と自分の行動を否定しています。同意の言葉だけを拾うと③に見えます。逆に Wren を「注意する側だからもともと返している」と決めつけると①になります。
q36.trapNote: 同意はするが自分は動かない Beatriz と、注意する側だから元から守っていると思わせる Wren。前者を数えると③、後者を落とすと①。
